clue.text: Supreme commander drops northern woman — a chirpy creature

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so the commander loses a letter

blocks.note: C-in-C, Commander-in-Chief
N is the abbreviation for northern
a woman's name

explanation.surface: A top general dismisses a woman from the north and turns to a chirping insect.
explanation.walkthrough: C-in-C is the standard short form of Commander-in-Chief; removing its N leaves CIC before ADA.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is an insect famous for the loud shrill chirping song made by the males.

clue.text: Charge may include first instalment of reparations for bloomer

indicators.note: a first instalment is only the opening part, so one initial letter
include means hold within, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a cost is a charge
taken as written
the first letter of reparations

explanation.surface: A fee might cover the first payment of compensation for a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a mistake in British slang, but here it is anything that blooms, a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Costmary is an aromatic herb of the daisy family, a flowering plant once used to flavour ale.

clue.text: Root taken by tailless creature — little bird and antelope

indicators.note: without a tail, each creature loses its last letter

blocks.note: a chick is a baby bird
the oryx is a large antelope

explanation.surface: A root is eaten by some animal that has lost its tail, a bird or an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' applies to both the little bird and the antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicory root is roasted and ground as a coffee substitute, so the plant is known for its root.

clue.text: Liquor manufacturer's daughter is a sucker

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
a tiller is a shoot from the base of a plant, also called a sucker

explanation.surface: The whisky maker's daughter is a gullible soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', not a possessive. Sucker means a plant shoot, not a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A distiller makes spirits such as whisky or gin by distilling, a maker of liquor.

clue.text: Omnipresence of one left in university extremely briefly

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters only
in places one group of letters inside another

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
the outer letters of briefly
I is the Roman numeral one
quit means left, departed

explanation.surface: Someone who walked out of university almost at once is oddly described as everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One left' reads as I QUIT, and it sits between the B and Y of briefly, after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubiquity is the state of seeming to be found everywhere at the same time, which is what omnipresence names.

clue.text: Means of subsistence Werther's Charlotte went on cutting

blocks.note: first meaning: one's basic livelihood
second meaning: what Charlotte kept slicing in Thackeray's poem

explanation.walkthrough: Thackeray's comic poem 'The Sorrows of Werther' ends with Charlotte, unmoved by Werther's death, going on cutting this.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary everyday living is called this, and it is also the plain food Charlotte kept slicing.

clue.text: Game nobody abandons on even terms

indicators.note: abandons means leaves behind, so a letter is dropped from the game

blocks.note: quoits is a ring-throwing game
O, zero, stands for nobody

explanation.surface: A game everyone quits ends up a draw.
explanation.definitionFit: To be quits is to be square with someone, neither owing the other, after settling a debt.

clue.text: Uncouth redhead in sick-bed

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the bed

blocks.note: ill means sick
taken as written
the head, or first letter, of red

explanation.surface: A rude ginger-haired patient lies in his hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Redhead reads as one word for a ginger person, but splits into red and its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-bred describes someone badly brought up, showing poor manners, which is what uncouth means.

clue.text: Sheriffs assistants longing to receive key award

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the longing holds the other letters

blocks.note: a yen is a longing
E is a musical key
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Deputies in a western long for a prestigious prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Key is a musical key here, giving the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen were attendants of a sheriff in old England, as in the yeomen in Robin Hood tales.

clue.text: Revolutionary device used in celebrating a failed plot

definitions.text: Revolutionary device used in celebrating a failed plot

blocks.note: surface reading: a weapon of political revolutionaries
setter's reading: a spinning firework set off on Bonfire Night, 5 November, marking the foiled Gunpowder Plot

explanation.surface: Radicals mark the anniversary of a failed conspiracy with some contraption.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary means spinning round, not rebellious. Britain marks Guy Fawkes' failed 1605 plot with fireworks every 5 November.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catherine wheel is a pinned firework that spins as it burns, a staple of Bonfire Night displays.

clue.text: Well-ordered fruit found by chance in Kent

indicators.note: in places the fruit and chance inside the county's letters

blocks.note: hips are the fruit of the rose
hap is an old word for chance or luck
Kent is in the South East of England

explanation.surface: Neat fruit stumbled upon by luck in a Kentish orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in England's South East, so it stands for the compass abbreviation; hap is an archaic word for luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape is an idiom from sailing meaning trim, tidy and in good order, as a ship should be kept.

clue.text: Retired soldier takes game home in Alaska

indicators.note: a retired soldier has withdrawn, so his letters go backwards

blocks.note: GI is an American soldier
loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: A veteran settles down with a card game in his Alaskan house.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is a card game as well as a lavatory, which the surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is the domed snow house built by Inuit peoples of the Arctic, including Alaska.

clue.text: Secure his conversion, like Othello

indicators.note: a conversion changes a thing into another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to moor a boat is to secure it
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A missionary aims to make sure of a convert, perhaps a Moor like Shakespeare's general.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice, so something like him is Moorish in character.

clue.text: Merit of French Bible used in diocese

indicators.note: used in places the Bible's letters inside the diocese

blocks.note: de is French for of
a see is a bishop's diocese
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A French Bible is judged worthy of use throughout a church district.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve it; both verbs mean to be worthy of a reward or punishment.

clue.text: A size of paper — imperial?

blocks.note: first meaning: a traditional paper size
second meaning: kingly, majestic

explanation.walkthrough: Royal and imperial are both old paper sizes, which is why the question mark is there: imperial is a synonym, not another size.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal names a traditional sheet size and also means regal or majestic, close in sense to imperial.

clue.text: Excellent sort of seat for opera left, perhaps

blocks.note: Wagner's Ring cycle of operas
left is an example of a side

explanation.surface: A theatregoer wants a fine seat at the opera, maybe on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat for opera' looks like a theatre booking, but the seat is the definition and the opera is Wagner's Ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringside seat is beside the boxing or circus ring, the best place to watch, hence excellent.

clue.text: Like a thistle, it's less harmful across a stream

definitions.note: the definition describes the plant: it is thistle-like

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the outer word stretches over the other

blocks.note: safer means less harmful
a flow is a stream

explanation.surface: Crossing a stream is gentler than tangling with a thistle.
explanation.definitionFit: Safflower is a thistle-like plant with orange flowers, grown for its oil and dye.

clue.text: Generosity with a capital letter, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means it is going by the spoken sound

blocks.note: a capital letter is a large one, here the letter S

explanation.surface: Kindness spelt with a capital, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: A capital is an upper-case letter; spoken as large S, which letter it is falls out of the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is liberal giving of money or gifts, open-handed kindness to others.

clue.text: In its turn it may ensure our entry

definitions.text: In its turn it may ensure our entry

blocks.clueFragment: In its turn it may ensure our entry
blocks.note: surface reading: something that, when its time comes, guarantees we are admitted
setter's reading: the object is literally turned by hand to open a door

explanation.surface: Taking turns, each thing in sequence secures our admission somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In its turn' sounds like 'when its time comes', but means 'when it is rotated'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorknob is the round handle you rotate to release the latch, letting you go into a room.

clue.text: Vehicle serving several purposes at once

blocks.note: first meaning: the original full name of a bus
second meaning: comprising many items

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one description of a multi-purpose vehicle; in fact the words split into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnibus is the full name of a bus, and as an adjective it means covering many things together.

clue.text: Young deer, say, a member of this classification

indicators.note: say asks us to go by how the word is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: a fawn is a young deer; the rural god faun is pronounced the same
taken as written

explanation.surface: A baby deer is offered as one example from this group.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly true: a fawn is indeed one of the animals in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the collective term for the animal life of a region, a classification set beside flora.

clue.text: Made one mad in feud about island

indicators.note: mad suggests wild disorder, so these letters are scrambled
about means around, so the scrambled letters surround another

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone becomes furious in a quarrel over an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To unify is to make into one whole, so the past tense equals made one.

clue.text: Her youngster is kept outside, being in the second order

indicators.note: kept outside means the second word is placed around the first

blocks.note: a cub is a young animal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother leaves her child outdoors and the household drops to second place.
explanation.walkthrough: In medieval angelology cherubim rank second of the nine orders, after the seraphim.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angel of the second of the nine traditional orders in the heavenly hierarchy.

clue.text: Cutter also observed in receding rough water

indicators.note: receding means moving back, so the water's letters run backwards
observed in means seen inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: and means also
wash is the rough water left by a boat

explanation.surface: A boat called the Cutter was also spotted in the choppy wake of an ebb tide.
explanation.walkthrough: A cutter is also a kind of boat, which fits the water picture; here it is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsaw is a carpenter's saw worked with one hand, a tool for cutting wood.

clue.text: A Scotsman is climbing this mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read from the bottom up

blocks.note: Ian is a typical Scottish name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot is scaling a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai in Egypt is the mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments in the Bible.

clue.text: Striking occupation for election officials

blocks.note: first meaning: forceful, effective
second meaning: counting the votes, the work of tellers

explanation.walkthrough: Tellers are the officials who count votes, so their job is the counting itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling blow is effective and striking; telling is also an old word for counting, as votes are counted.

clue.text: Hood or sash worn by sailors?

indicators.note: something worn is wrapped round the wearer, so the sailors enclose the sash

blocks.note: RN is the Royal Navy
an obi is a Japanese sash

explanation.surface: Sailors choose between a hood and a sash as part of their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Hood is not headgear but the outlaw Robin Hood, named by his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is the first name of Hood, the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest, so one stands for the other.

clue.text: Plant obtained from wise characters in Leeds works

indicators.note: works suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant bred by clever people at a factory in Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' signals that the letters of the two words are used, not their meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a small white alpine flowering plant, the national emblem associated with Switzerland and Austria.

clue.text: But could this fortress be blown apart by a single shot?

definitions.text: But could this fortress be blown apart by a single shot?

indicators.note: blown apart means split open, with the other letters filling the gap

blocks.note: taken as written, then split
a still is a single photographic shot

explanation.surface: A doubter asks whether a famous prison could really have fallen to one bullet.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'could' stresses doubt: the fortress was stormed by a crowd, not one shot. A shot here is a photograph, a still.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress and prison stormed in 1789 at the start of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Grand Dickensian character's feeling of resentment

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
Barnaby Rudge, title hero of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A splendid figure from Dickens is said to nurse a resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand looks like a description of the character but is slang for a thousand, abbreviated G.
explanation.definitionFit: A grudge is a lasting ill will held against someone for a past wrong or insult.
